take: Dropbox demonstrates a persistent central All files area that mixes shared, team, and other folders, but not reuse within courses.
observed: Global navigation includes All files and Shared. All files shows search, Upload or drop, Create folder, Recents and Starred filters, and suggested shared/team folders.
limits: Single screen; no course attachment flow, second usage of one asset, version propagation, copy/reference semantics, replacement, or deletion impact is shown.

take: Canva lets an instructor choose an existing design from the central Projects hierarchy and explicitly copy it into or move it into the current course.
observed: From the course, open Add new; choose Choose design; browse Your projects and open a project; select a design; choose Copy to course or Move. The final frame shows the selected presentations as ordered course activities with Resource type and access indicators.
limits: Six sampled frames do not show whether a copied activity remains linked to the source, whether later edits propagate, whether the same design is attached to multiple courses, or how replacement and deletion work.
secondary_relevance: Q2: the final course view demonstrates an ordered activity list, but the flow's distinctive evidence is library-to-course reuse and explicit copy-versus-move semantics.
